findings.title: Normalize teacher-scope equality and draft identity across retained and legacy scene readers
findings.trigger: Load a student through the new retained reader, then reconcile a stale activity review or parent draft through the unchanged legacy GET callback. A second trigger is adopting a legacy GET scene after clinic/observation reconciliation while a workspace draft is unsaved.
findings.actual: canonicalJson sorts teacherScope to actorId,ownerId. The legacy TeacherQueries scene inserts ownerId,actorId. teacherWorkspaceView compares JSON.stringify(scope), so equal actors are refused as teacher_scene_actor_conflict. Its draft map keys also stringify the whole scope object, so the same logical draft receives a second memory key when a legacy scene is adopted.
findings.expected: Identical ownerId/actorId/student/workspace identity must reconcile successfully and retain the same unsaved or pending draft regardless of JSON property order or read transport.
findings.impact: Both activity and parent-draft recovery can be blocked for an unchanged teacher. Switching scene readers hides unsaved text in a separate in-memory draft entry. No permanent stored-data loss or duplicated real write was exercised or claimed.
findings.repair: Reuse sameTeacherScope for value-based equality and use a stable tuple of ownerId, actorId, studentId, and workspace identity for draft keys. Audit equivalent scope-object keys in affected views. Either route remaining scene reads through the shared reader or preserve compatibility with both formats; changing only the initial loader is insufficient.
findings.validationRequired: Synthetic actual-view tests must cover retained-to-legacy reconciliation, preservation of edited draft text and pending request identity across both scene formats, and rejection when owner or actor values actually change.

findings.title: Validate the complete retained page envelope before accepting its document
findings.trigger: A transport callback supplies otherwise valid JSON and document digest, recalculates serializedBytes, but uses exhausted:'false' on a terminal page, omits callerBinding or coverage, changes effects.sourceWrites to true, or returns an empty retrievedAt.
findings.actual: readRetainedDocument resolves successfully in each case. The checks only cover selected fields; terminal detection uses truthiness, and snapshot verification authenticates neither the page metadata nor its schema. The generic return value hides the rejected-or-missing coverage/effect metadata from the consumer.
findings.expected: Reject malformed or contradictory academy.retained-query.v1 envelopes before returning a trusted retained document, including exact boolean continuation state and required binding, provenance, coverage and read-only effect fields.
findings.impact: The shared transport boundary accepts incomplete or contradictory pages, so a provider regression or mixed contract version can be presented to web/CLI consumers as a successful retained read. This is not a demonstrated authentication bypass or source write.
findings.repair: Add a browser-safe runtime validator for the declared reply union. Validate required fields and scalar types, hash/binding shape, finite safe page counters, boolean exhausted, continuation consistency, coverage constants and false effect flags before accumulation. Preserve the existing content digest and replay checks.
findings.validationRequired: Repeat these malformed cases with correct serializedBytes and a valid document hash. Each must fail with a bounded contract refusal/error, while genuine server pages and established legacy consumer semantics continue to work.
